items.body: The most useful thing about the pelican riding a bicycle test continues to be illustrating the differences between models in the same family running at different effort levels - here's Gemini 4 Carbon, the new Gemini 4 Neon, and Gemini 4 Hydrogen at low, medium, and high

comments.text: https://t.co/s32nlEakl5
carbon low already had the sailor hat, the scarf and the basket for 9 cents. high spent another 11 cents and 2.5 extra minutes to put a fish in the basket
comments.text_zh: Carbon 低档已经有了水手帽、围巾和篮子，才花 9 美分。高档又多花了 11 美分和额外 2.5 分钟，往篮子里放了一条鱼

comments.text: Watching Neon scale from low to high effort is wild—it goes from a surrealist blob to actually getting the foot-to-pedal mechanics right.
comments.text_zh: 看 Neon 从低努力拉到高努力真的很夸张——它会从超现实主义的一团，变成真的把脚踩踏板的机械关系做对。

comments.text: this is so cool!
Effort level is becoming as important a knob as model choice. Would love to see token count or latency next to each pelican, since that's the real trade-off when picking low vs high.
comments.text_zh: 努力程度正在变成和选模型一样重要的旋钮。很希望在每只鹈鹕旁边看到 token 数或延迟，因为选低档还是高档时，真正的取舍就在这里。

comments.text: Which jump actually changed the bike, low to medium or medium to high?
comments.text_zh: 到底是哪一档变化真正改了那辆自行车，是低到中，还是中到高？

comments.text: Gemini 4 这几个 effort 档位差别主要在哪，token 数还是推理步数？
nice way to show the differences
wait so neon is the priciest of the 3 until carbon doubles dec 1?? google naming is cooked lol, does high neon beat low carbon tho
comments.text_zh: 等等，所以在 Carbon 12 月 1 日涨价一倍之前，Neon 是这三个里最贵的？？Google 这命名也太离谱了哈哈，那高档 Neon 能胜过低档 Carbon 吗

comments.text: Holding the prompt fixed and only varying effort level is a clean way to see what extra reasoning actually buys. Do the low-effort versions mostly miss on structure (frame, wheels) or on fine details?
comments.text_zh: 把提示词固定、只改努力程度，能很干净地看出额外推理到底换来了什么。低努力版本主要是漏掉结构（车架、轮子），还是漏在细枝末节上？

items.body: Here's GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol for "Make a three js animation where yonkers stands up as a big mech (cool stand up motion) and stomps around manhattan and queens and Brooklyn, use openstreetmap mapping data" https://t.co/oRZT2zMByi

comments.text: dare i say sol won here
A giant mech casually stomping around Manhattan was not on my bingo card today — and it actually looks great 😄
Astra vs Sol on the same prompt is a useful A/B — did one handle the OpenStreetMap data better? Our index has Astra at 62; the mech test is a fun way to see if the score shows in the output.
Wondering how adeptly the model navigated through those nuanced geometries of the boroughs.
The OpenStreetMap part is the real test here. Making a mech look cool is easy, getting it to stomp down the right streets means the model actually had to wire up real data.
这个机甲 three.js 测试很有代表性：同样一个提示词，创意代码类任务最考验的不是单次最强，而是反复迭代的成本。你下面那条说 Fable 最打动你的是把 Yonkers

mech yonkers is the fun part. the dev signal is whether it reasoned about the scene or just pattern-matched a cool description. three.js is mostly coordinates, so bad geometry shows anyway. did astra and sol actually differ here, or both basically nail it? #AI
This is the test I trust, one prompt on two models, side by side. I will do the same with Astra and Sol on a coding task I already run, then look at retries and the review time.

Tip for anyone repeating this test: save the OpenStreetMap data as a GeoJSON extract first and give both models the same file. Live Overpass queries add rate limits and randomness, so you end up comparing the API, not the models.

items.body:
I shipped a new version of Datasette Lite recently - my build of the Datasette Python web app that runs entirely in the browser with WebAssembly and Pyodide - here's what's new and how it all works
https://t.co/MXSF8Sus79

comments.text: datasette fully in the browser never stops feeling like a magic trick
a full python web app running in the browser still feels like magic. curious how you handle sqlite file size limits with pyodide
the URL pins the SQLite version too. “works on my machine” ok here’s my url

Knowing where a file gets processed helps people decide which data to open. We’d put that explanation beside the import button, including which actions keep data on the device and which send it elsewhere.
Running the full server-side Datasette in the browser via service workers and Pyodide is a neat trick — what's the practical limit first, dataset size or query speed?
Running the whole thing in-browser with Pyodide is pretty neat. No server to set up either.

For a SQL exercise, I'd link to a starting query and keep the solution in a separate link. Readers could change one WHERE clause and see the consequence, rather than spending the first half of the lesson installing Python.

Running a full server-side Python app locally in the browser via service workers, WebAssembly and Pyodide is such a clean offline-first architecture. Really appreciate the technical breakdown, learned a lot!
Running the whole thing in the browser is so underrated for small business tools. No server, no install, the client opens a link and the data never leaves their PC.
Running the whole app in the browser is great for sharing data people shouldn't have to install anything to explore. Curious what the practical size limit is now before loading gets painful.

items.summary: I've been exploring new ways to sandbox code written by coding agents - here's a description of the external sandbox pattern, where agents run on your Mac but execute code in a WebAssembly or QEMU or…
items.body: I've been exploring new ways to sandbox code written by coding agents - here's a description of the external sandbox pattern, where agents run on your Mac but execute code in a WebAssembly or QEMU or Apple Container sandbox - with demos for Claude Code, Codex and Pi

comments.text: Keeping the agent local while making the VM’s two escape routes explicit feels like a clean boundary.
comments.text_zh: 让智能体保持本地运行，同时明确虚拟机的两条逃逸路径，感觉像是一条清晰的边界。

comments.text: Filesystem syncing between the host and the guest sandbox usually becomes the main latency bottleneck once an agent starts doing rapid edit and test loops.
comments.text_zh: 一旦智能体开始快速进行编辑和测试循环，主机与客户沙箱之间的文件系统同步通常会成为主要的延迟瓶颈。

comments.text: The gap I keep hitting with this pattern: the sandbox covers code the agent executes, but the agent's own tools (file read/edit, web fetch, MCP calls) still run in the host process with your user's permissions. So you end up needing two policies, not one.
comments.text_zh: 我反复遇到的这种模式的缺口：沙箱覆盖了智能体执行的代码，但智能体自身的工具（文件读取/编辑、网页抓取、MCP 调用）仍然以你的用户权限在主机进程中运行。所以你最终需要两套策略，而不是一套。

comments.text: heads up claude code people, only bash goes in the box. read and edit still touch your real files
comments.text_zh: 提醒使用 Claude Code 的朋友们，只有 bash 会被放进沙箱。读取和编辑仍然会触碰你的真实文件

comments.text: The first sandbox I'd trust with real files keeps the agent on my Mac and the code where it can't touch anything.
comments.text_zh: 第一个我敢用来处理真实文件的沙箱，让智能体留在我的 Mac 上，而代码则放在无法触碰任何东西的地方。

comments.text: Keeping the agent running locally while offloading untrusted execution to an external Linux VM with a controlled proxy is such an elegant architecture. Really practical balance between safety and developer workflow 🛠️
comments.text_zh: 让智能体在本地运行，同时将不受信任的执行卸载到带有受控代理的外部 Linux 虚拟机，这是一种非常优雅的架构。在安全性和开发者工作流之间实现了非常实用的平衡 🛠️

comments.text: what's the biggest challenge you've faced when trying to implement this pattern in practice?
comments.text_zh: 你在实践中尝试实现这种模式时遇到的最大挑战是什么？

comments.text: yes, this index is the best part — one place to see all the sandbox implementations side by side instead of hunting repos
comments.text_zh: 是的，这个索引是最棒的部分——在一个地方就能并排查看所有沙箱实现，而不用到处翻找仓库

comments.text: how much slower is Apple Container than running it straight on the Mac? that's the bit that decides if I'd actually leave it on
comments.text_zh: Apple Container 比直接在 Mac 上运行慢多少？这才是决定我是否真的会一直开着它的关键

comments.text: A reusable execution sandbox could let hardening work benefit several coding agents at once. That’s an appealing payoff from making the boundary independent of the agent
comments.text_zh: 一个可复用的执行沙箱可以让加固工作同时惠及多个编码智能体。让边界独立于智能体，这是一个很有吸引力的回报
